title: The Stamp Beneath the Signature
subtitle: Clue · GM clue · physical fact, discovery and implication

fields.label: Observable fact
fields.value: On the duplicate roll, the debtor-name ink crosses the witness stamp's dried ridge without being indented by it: the names were written after the stamp was applied. This establishes sequence, not authorship or intent.

fields.label: Ways to discover
fields.value: Compare the original and carbon copy at the Archive; inspect the layering with Ledgerglass; or ask Pell to demonstrate how the Office press leaves its ridge. These are alternative channels for one clue.

fields.label: Inference / next action
fields.value: Office rules require witnesses to certify the completed named roll and demand fresh certification for later name changes. The layering therefore raises a specific recertification defect; check the witness register or ask Ansel. If no fresh certification exists, request a stay. Question the countersigner or obtain the earlier impression to investigate responsibility.

fields.label: What it does NOT prove
fields.value: It does not by itself identify who changed the roll. Nera's receipt and Vale's countersignature independently connect the commissioner.

fields.label: Roll policy
fields.value: If the ridge is plainly demonstrated, give the fact. A relevant roll may reveal it more quickly or create an advantage for the hearing, not decide whether the entire mystery remains solvable.
